target_customer: Busy families and working parents who want a quick home-cooked dinner
problem: Parents want fresh home-cooked dinners but lack time for shopping and prep.
business_model: Subscription meal kit delivery with prepped ingredients

founders.name: Ooshma Garg
previous_startups: An earlier business started from her Stanford dorm room (unnamed in the source)
founders.background_notes: Gobble's 10 year anniversary post describes her building a first business in 2010 and early ideas such as a local chef marketplace before the dinner kit. Later became a Visiting Group Partner at Y Combinator per a podcast listing.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operational: sourcing, prepping, cold chain logistics and fulfillment, plus a menu personalization 'taste engine' on top of standard ordering software.

defensibility.rationale: Pre-chopped, par-cooked kits and chef recipes were differentiators, but Blue Apron, HelloFresh and Plated were similar and could add faster meals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established kits stayed separate; Gobble partnered with Walmart in 2018 and was bought by Intelligent Foods in December 2022.

market_need_then: Meal kits were an emerging category in 2014, and the YC post pitched a dinner kit made in 10 minutes in one pan; by October 2015 the company claimed about 1 million meals a year in California.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, family oriented, stated mission to create moments of love through food

branding.community_and_virality: Parents Magazine named it a top meal kit for families per the Intelligent Foods release; Walmart partnered with it in 2018.

brand_strength.rationale: A short real-word name that fits the product, with some press and retail partnership, but no sourced evidence of a brand asset driving growth.

pivots.from: Earlier ideas including a local chef marketplace and personalized catering
pivots.to: 15 minute meal kits, with first kits shipped August 2014
pivots.why: Gobble's anniversary post describes experiments before the 15 minute meal kit launch

outcome_analysis: Gobble found its model in the 2014 meal kit launch, raised a 10.75 million dollar Series A in October 2015 and a 15 million dollar Series B in October 2017, and was reported profitable in 2019. It sold to Intelligent Foods in December 2022 with Garg becoming CEO of Gobble and Sunbasket, a positive exit for a company that stayed smaller and leaner than Blue Apron or HelloFresh. Terms were not disclosed.
notes: Series B article says nearly 30 million total including a prior 14.8 million, so about 4 million of earlier seed money is unrecorded; ZoomInfo and PitchBook totals of 27.1 and 33 million are aggregator figures, unverified. Founding year not stated; first kits shipped August 2014. The profitability claim is from the acquirer's release. Acquisition date has a conflict between a 8 December 2022 release date (search snippet) and a 28 December 2022 article, so only the month is recorded. A Signalbase page dating it 2025 is disregarded. The YC page lists Garg only; competitors cite the YC blog source from the W14 period, whose text was seen via a search snippet.
